items.title: John Fedchock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 28, 2015
items.q: I listened to the Maynard Ferguson albums in the 70s when he was doing all the rock stuff

ctx.x: Did you ever have that — did you have a band or a — for you was it more the big bands?

That was my first inspiration, although I did listen to groups like that. I had Chicago records and Blood, Sweat & Tears records and things like that, and I got to work with Blood, Sweat & Tears when I moved to New York, a few times. But it was more the straight-ahead jazz that inspired me. And I’m not sure why that was but it was. I mean I liked all the more modern stuff. I listened to the Maynard Ferguson albums in the 70s when he was doing all the rock stuff and it was — a lot of that stuff was very…
& Tears had a lot of great jazz harmony, as did Chicago. But as far as the soloists go, they weren’t unleashed as much as they were in jazz.
